author: Grnchot
title: Oddly satisfying!
content:
Pretty innovative take on the pixel shooter genre. Instead of removing pixels from a flat image, you are slowly destroying a rotating 3D object. I gotta say I love watching the dismantling process, there's just something oddly satisfying about it.

The game mechanics seem really polished - the controls, interacting with the 3D model, everything feels pretty smooth.

Kudos to the graphics designer too, the subtle lighting on the little cubes as you rotate the model really makes them feel solid.

It's not just the looks though, you get a nice mental challenge as well, especially on the Super Hard levels.

Of course, you have to watch an ad after each level, but that's pretty much expected for these types of games.

As long as they don't start showing ads in the middle of a level (which is an instant uninstall for me), I'm happy to take a breather and watch ads between levels.

And of course, you don’t earn enough by passing a level for it to be worthwhile (like 50 coins per level yet 900 to continue?). 

The ads in and of themselves aren’t horrible, it’s just you end up having to watch a few each level to pass it (at least any level marked “hard”). And even then, of course they limit the number of ads  one can watch per day. At that point the only hope you have of passing is paying (real world dollars) or waiting until the next day.

Original:  Game’s core mechanics and fuel are a lot of fun. Provide some light puzzle elements, Weil just being a very satisfying game. However, as other people have noted, there are bugged in which the wrong number of cubes of specific colors are in the puzzle. It seems inconsistent as to exactly what this is, so maybe it’s a software bug rather than a puzzle bug. For example, on puzzle 86, I played through it once, and there were three blocks of the wrong color at the end. I had three orange blocks remaining, and a shooter that was pink with three shots remaining. I tried it again, and this time same thing happened, except I only had one extra unpaired block. Hopefully they can fix this, I was getting close to buying it, but I seen some of these concerns, and was nervous about doing so.
